name: Kanggape
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and Typological Studies in Languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19 (covers Igom/Kanggape; phonology notes).
earlier_scan.note: Survey-level phonology notes may include stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kang1291 (Kanggape); references listed: Z'graggen 1969 (pp. 149-151), Z'graggen 1971, Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment).

Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp. DOI 10.25911/5d739250d08c9.
sources.note: Same disclaimer as the 1971 book, pp. 13-14: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Nothing Igom-specific on stress.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu Basin. In A. Pawley, R. Attenborough, J. Golson & R. Hide (eds), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Comparative/historical; Igom appears only in Proto-Watam-Awar-Gamay/Ramu cognate tables and a data-sources line ('Igom: Capell (1952); Z'graggen (1972)'). No mention of stress for Igom or any Ramu language.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. 179 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19.
sources.note: General disclaimer for the whole survey, p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Igom section (2.23.21.12, p. 80) gives villages, history of record (Holtker 1937b; Capell 1952:141ff notes + wordlist) and lexicostatistics only; no Igom stress or phonology statement; no stress diacritics anywhere in the text.
Classification and Ethnologue population only; nothing on phonology or stress.
